1980 BRIGHT GRADES AND CROPS \( ^{1} \)  (J. C. Crump, M. Wood)

DATE OF REPORT: May 7, 1982

Grades 4, 33, 67 and 78 taken from the Georgia, Eastern, Southern and Old Belts have been studied at various RH conditions at \(75^{\circ}\mathrm{F}\). The dependency of OV and CV on RH was found to vary only slightly from sample to sample. The relationships between OV and RH and between CV and RH for each sample were found to agree well with those modeled by H. Hartung for 1978 DBC Bright having essentially the same slope and differing only in magnitude. A report will be issued.

CV-OV-RH RELATIONSHIPS OF ESB-3 AND ESB-1 \( ^{2} \)  (J. C. Crump)

Isothermal analyses of the CV-OV-RH relationships for ESB-3 at 75°F have been made. The results were found to vary slightly from those obtained previously for ESB-2. OV values taken within the RH range between 30% and 80% were consistently lower by an average 1.5 OV units for ESB-3 than for ESB-1. The corresponding CV values for ESB-3 averaged 8 CV units higher than for ESB-1. Their differences are greater than the variations of +0.5 OV units and +1.1 CV units found by taking duplicate measurements at each RH condition on each sample.

STIFFNESS AS A FUNCTION OF CURING \( ^{3} \)  (B. C. LaRoy)

Further analysis of data from the stress relaxation of air- and flue-cured Bright and Burley leaf supports the following:

1. The air-cured Bright tobacco was significantly stiffer than other leaf at the same relative humidity (58%). This is consistent with D. Teng's CV results.

2. Air-cured leaf in which a large vein contributed to stiffness appeared to have a slightly different relaxation spectrum than flue-cured materials. For samples in which a large vein was not bent, no differences in relaxation spectrum were resolved, even though the air-cured Bright samples were stiffer. Thus, it seems likely that air-cured Bright is stiffened primarily by an increased number of mechanisms which are energetically similar to those found in the other materials.
